definition: In this historical psychiatric usage, intermission means a temporary interval or pause in the course of a disorder, during which symptoms lessen or are absent before returning. It refers to the illness progressing with breaks rather than in one continuous, unchanging state.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Doubting Mania; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports that the disorder “progresses usually with periods of intermission,” but it does not explicitly support the added claim that symptoms “lessen or are absent before returning.”

The phrasing “in this historical psychiatric usage” is acceptable, but the definition slightly generalizes beyond the source by turning a course description into a fuller clinical gloss that the packet does not state directly.
The packet only states that the disorder “progresses usually with periods of intermission”; it does not define intermission as a time when “symptoms lessen or are absent.”
The packet does not support the additional framing that the illness “progress[es] with breaks rather than in one continuous, unchanging state,” beyond the brief mention of “periods of intermission.”
